title: 2015 Space Year Ballad
about: A full reflection on my first State Arts-In year, where tech work, friendships, pranks, hidden paths, and small traditions changed me.
description: This track brings together the full story of my 2015 Space Year. I arrived as a quiet, sheltered fifteen-year-old and joined the Tech Crew without knowing where I fit. Over the month, Mama Jasinta showed me the hidden fair, Greg and I rebuilt spaceships, Tony and I melted screws, Jules and I worked above the ramp, and countless invisible backstage jobs taught me what it meant to contribute. Code names, the nickname Ghost, pull-string fireworks, Duck Duck Grey Duck, breakfast towers, the Showboat, and the friendships around them all became pieces of the same transformation. I came to help build a spaceship, but what I carried home was confidence, experience, and another family.
lyrics: Verse 1
I was fifteen, quiet, homeschooled, Walking through the gates
alone. State Arts In was Space Year, Though it felt like another world
I’d never known. The stages buzzed with music, The midway never slept. I
joined the Tech Crew with a hammer, And wondered where I fit.
Chorus
It was Space Year, Boards and laughter everywhere. A nervous kid
came looking For a place to lend a hand. It was Space Year, More than
anyone could see. I came to build a spaceship… A family was building me.
Verse 2
Mama Jasinta found the newcomers Like ducklings needing home.
She showed us hidden hallways, Backstage stairs and rooftop domes. The
green room, light shelf, secret paths, Cheap meals and places free. She
taught us how to cross the fair Long before it welcomed me.
Chorus
It was Space Year, Boards and laughter everywhere. A nervous kid
came looking For a place to lend a hand. It was Space Year, More than
anyone could see. I came to build a spaceship… A family was building me.
Verse 3
Greg let me join his project After Mike said, “Find some more.”
Five times Paul said, “Build again,” Till we knew every single board.
Canvas waited patiently While frames rose, fell, then rose. The
spaceship wasn’t all we built— Friendship started to grow.
Chorus
It was Space Year, Boards and laughter everywhere. A nervous kid
came looking For a place to lend a hand. It was Space Year, More than
anyone could see. I came to build a spaceship… A family was building me.
Verse 4
Tony and I fought stubborn walls, Melted screw heads in the
heat. Jules and I climbed crooked ladders With empty air beneath our
feet. Extension cords and light boxes, Work no audience would know. The
show could only shine Because of hands behind the show.
Chorus
It was Space Year, Boards and laughter everywhere. A nervous kid
came looking For a place to lend a hand. It was Space Year, More than
anyone could see. I came to build a spaceship… A family was building me.
Verse 5
The radios all crackled With names we’d made for fun. Hawker,
Gold Leader, Twinkie, Crispy Kreme as one. Then somebody called me
Ghost. The nickname somehow stayed. Not because I disappeared— Because I
quietly drifted away.
Chorus
It was Space Year, Boards and laughter everywhere. A nervous kid
came looking For a place to lend a hand. It was Space Year, More than
anyone could see. I came to build a spaceship… A family was building me.
Verse 6
Greg and I tied pull-string fireworks Where bunks and fans would
spring. Dorm staff searched for culprits, But couldn’t prove a thing.
Duck Duck Grey Duck filled the roadway, Police lights filled the night.
Christoph feared my mother’s anger. She smiled and said, “Thank
you.”—just right.
Chorus
It was Space Year, Boards and laughter everywhere. A nervous kid
came looking For a place to lend a hand. It was Space Year, More than
anyone could see. I came to build a spaceship… A family was building me.
Verse 7
Caitlin and Mitch laughed kindly At how innocent I’d been. One
afternoon they showed me The wider world I’d never seen. Breakfast
milk-carton towers, Tables chanting back and forth, Tiny traditions that
seemed ordinary Are now worth so much more.
Chorus
It was Space Year, Boards and laughter everywhere. A nervous kid
came looking For a place to lend a hand. It was Space Year, More than
anyone could see. I came to build a spaceship… A family was building me.
Verse 8
We walked the old Showboat, Not knowing it was the last. Titanic
photos on the bow Became treasures of the past. The fair packed up its
stages, The lights all faded blue. But every memory stayed alive Because
of people I once knew.
Bridge
Some years teach through classrooms. Some years teach through
life. Some years fit inside a month Yet change you for all time.
Final Chorus
It was Space Year, The year my life turned west. A quiet
kid found courage Working with the very best. It was Space Year, The
beginning of my road. I came to build a spaceship, But carried home far
more.
Outro
The stages came apart. The fairgrounds settled down. The code
names faded into memory, Yet I still hear their sound. If someone asks
what changed me, The answer’s simple and true: I came to build a
spaceship… I left with another family, too.
